_label: Odyssey I DISCOVERY, LIGHT PASS. Domain-different specimen: DNA/genomic, not natural language.

identity.checkpoint_format: raw PyTorch .pt (pickle), NOT safetensors -- no cheap exact byte/tensor accounting available without a torch load

domain.modality: DNA / genomic sequence, autoregressive -- NOT natural language. Tokenization is over DNA bases, not a text vocabulary. The single most domain-different specimen in the whole ModelLake census this session ran -- every other specimen (55 total, 45 censused) is a text/vision/audio/multimodal LANGUAGE-adjacent model.

architecture_README_VERIFIED.family: StripedHyena2 -- Arc Institute's own hybrid architecture (per config.json's architecture field and public naming; internal operator-level structure NOT verified this pass -- would need either the paper or a loaded model to confirm gated-convolution/Hyena-operator/attention layer placement the way this session verified RWKV7/LFM2's structure directly from weights).
architecture_README_VERIFIED.max_training_context: up to 1,000,000 tokens (per README's checkpoint table) -- BY FAR the longest context of any specimen in this session's census (next longest: Dream-v0's 131072). Architecturally this IS StripedHyena2's whole design point: efficient long-range modeling for genomic sequences, which are naturally far longer than typical text documents.

byte_accounting_HONEST_LIMITS.finding: the naive filesize/2 estimate does NOT cleanly match the README's stated 7B (a 1.7% gap) -- unlike every safetensors specimen this session verified to within ~1%. Most likely explanation (NOT confirmed): a raw .pt checkpoint commonly bundles optimizer state, fp32 master-weight copies, or other non-inference data alongside the bf16 weights -- exactly the kind of 'complete system' accounting question the Byte Elimination Law asks about, but here the answer requires actually opening the pickle (gated) rather than a free header read.

failure_modes_not_yet_tested: Everything beyond config+README -- this is a deliberately light static pass; a real discovery pass needs either a torch-metadata-only load (state_dict keys without materializing tensors, still CPU-cheap but was not attempted this pass) or a full GPU/CPU load (gated).
preliminary_disposition: RESEARCH SPECIMEN, DEFERRED DEPTH. Genuinely the highest-information-diversity specimen in the lake (different domain entirely), but this pass could not cheaply get the same exact-byte rigor as the safetensors specimens. Next step if pursued further: a torch state_dict KEY listing (no tensor materialization) rather than a full load, which would still be cheap/CPU-only and would answer the byte-accounting gap above.
